program.title: Solanar Professional Meteorology Certificate
program.prerequisite: Successful completion of Solanar Professional Meteorology Certificate Year I or documented equivalent preparation.

courses.title: Dynamical Meteorology I
courses.description: Scale analysis; rotating-fluid dynamics; geostrophic and gradient wind; thermal wind; vorticity, divergence, vertical motion, baroclinicity and quasigeostrophic diagnosis.

courses.title: Synoptic & Mesoscale Analysis I
courses.description: Fronts, cyclogenesis, jet dynamics, potential-vorticity thinking, mesoscale boundaries and integrated surface/upper-air diagnosis.

courses.title: Ordinary Differential Equations for Atmospheric Science
courses.description: First- and second-order ODEs, systems, stability, numerical integration and atmospheric applications.

courses.title: Radar, Satellite & Remote Sensing II
courses.description: Doppler radar, dual-polarization concepts, multispectral satellite analysis, derived products, sampling limits and quality control.

courses.title: Numerical Weather Prediction I
courses.description: Model formulation, grids, discretization, initialization, parameterization, verification and forecast-system limitations.

courses.title: Operational Forecast Laboratory I
courses.description: Daily analysis, forecast preparation, uncertainty, verification, briefing and decision-support practice.

weeks.title: Scale Analysis & Equations of Atmospheric Motion

days.lesson: Derive the force terms in the horizontal momentum equations and use scale analysis to identify dominant balances at synoptic and mesoscale scales.
Review first-order ordinary differential equations, dimensional analysis, nondimensional numbers and characteristic time/length scales.
Diagnose which forces matter most in contrasting synoptic, tropical and mesoscale flow regimes.
Compare observed winds with model pressure/geopotential fields and identify where simple balance assumptions fail.
Produce a 24-hour forecast discussion that explicitly states the assumed dynamical balance and where ageostrophic effects may matter.
Develop geostrophic, gradient and cyclostrophic balances and connect curvature and pressure-gradient forces to real flow.
Solve linear first-order ODEs and vector-component problems; calculate geostrophic wind from height/pressure gradients.
Compare observed wind with geostrophic/gradient-wind estimates around highs, lows and strongly curved flow.
Use upper-air analyses and model fields to identify supergradient/subgradient and ageostrophic regions.
Brief expected wind evolution and identify locations where balanced-wind assumptions are least reliable.
Connect hydrostatic balance, hypsometric thickness and thermal-wind relationships to horizontal temperature gradients and vertical shear.
Solve separable ODEs and hydrostatic integrations; calculate thickness and thermal-wind vectors.
Analyze thickness, temperature advection and vertical shear on a multi-level synoptic case.
Compare sounding and model-derived thermal-wind structure with satellite cloud patterns.
Create a baroclinic-zone briefing with expected jet/front evolution and temperature-advection impacts.
Develop relative/planetary/absolute vorticity, divergence and stretching/tilting concepts and link them to vertical motion.
Work systems of ODEs and finite-difference estimates of divergence and vorticity from gridded wind data.
Compute qualitative vorticity/divergence tendencies from upper-air fields and connect them to ascent/descent.
Use model vorticity, divergence and vertical-motion products while documenting diagnostic limitations.
Issue a forecast discussion connecting upper forcing to sensible weather without treating one diagnostic as deterministic.
Use QG height-tendency/omega concepts, differential vorticity advection and thermal advection to diagnose large-scale vertical motion.
Apply second-order ODE concepts, boundary conditions and qualitative elliptic-equation reasoning to atmospheric diagnosis.
Construct a multi-field QG ascent/descent diagnosis from 500-hPa vorticity, thickness and temperature advection.
Compare QG diagnosis with model omega, precipitation and satellite evolution.
Prepare a precipitation/ceiling forecast tied to physically consistent forcing rather than model precipitation alone.

weeks.title: UNIT V CHECKPOINT — Dynamics & Diagnostic Reasoning

days.lesson: Synthesize Weeks 1–5: scale analysis, balanced flow, thermal wind, vorticity/divergence and QG vertical-motion diagnosis.
Cumulative ODE/vector/differential-diagnostic assessment with atmospheric applications.
Complete an unseen synoptic case with defensible force/vertical-motion diagnosis.
Cross-check model, radar/satellite and observations for consistency and identify contradictions.
Deliver a 7-minute technical forecast briefing and defend the dynamical reasoning. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.
Study kinematic frontogenesis/frontolysis, deformation, convergence, tilting and ageostrophic frontal circulations.
Apply deformation tensors/vector gradients and ODE stability ideas to frontal strengthening/weakening.
Analyze a surface/upper-air frontal zone and diagnose temperature/moisture advection and frontogenesis.
Use radar/satellite and model cross-sections to evaluate frontal slope, clouds and precipitation bands.
Forecast frontal timing, precipitation type/intensity and wind shifts with explicit timing uncertainty.
Connect baroclinic development, upper waves, surface pressure falls, occlusion and cyclone life-cycle frameworks.
Use coupled first-order systems and tendency reasoning to connect upper forcing with surface response.
Track cyclone evolution across successive analyses and identify deepening, occlusion and deformation zones.
Compare deterministic/ensemble cyclone tracks and satellite signatures of development.
Produce a 48-hour cyclone forecast with wind, precipitation and uncertainty corridors.

weeks.title: Jet Streaks, Ageostrophic Circulations & Rapid Development

days.lesson: Diagnose straight/curved jet streaks, entrance/exit regions, ageostrophic flow and coupling with lower-level baroclinic zones.
Use vector projections and second-order differential relationships to quantify along-/cross-jet components.
Analyze jet-level wind, divergence and surface development in a rapidly evolving case.
Compare water-vapor imagery, model tropopause/jet fields and observed cyclone deepening.
Brief high-impact wind and precipitation risks associated with jet/front coupling.
Introduce Ertel potential vorticity, conservation/invertibility concepts and dynamic-tropopause interpretation.
Work conservation-law ODEs and transformations; relate stratification and vorticity to PV changes.
Identify PV anomalies and tropopause folds in upper-air/model analyses and connect them to surface development.
Compare water-vapor imagery with PV/tropopause products and stratospheric intrusions.
Use PV thinking as one component of a multi-source forecast diagnosis and state limitations.
Study drylines, sea-breeze fronts, outflow boundaries, terrain circulations and mesoscale convergence zones.
Apply coordinate transformations, slope/gradient calculations and time-scale analysis to mesoscale motion.
Map mesoscale boundaries from surface observations and identify favored zones for ascent/convective initiation.
Use high-resolution model guidance, radar and satellite loops to track boundary evolution.
Issue a short-fuse mesoscale forecast emphasizing boundary timing and uncertainty.

weeks.title: UNIT VI CHECKPOINT — Synoptic & Mesoscale Weather Systems

days.lesson: Synthesize Weeks 7–11: fronts, cyclogenesis, jets, PV and mesoscale boundaries.
Cumulative vector/ODE/diagnostic calculations from an unseen weather-system case.
Complete a full surface-to-tropopause analysis and defend the expected evolution.
Reconcile radar, satellite, observations, deterministic models and ensembles.
Deliver an operational forecast shift briefing. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.

weeks.title: Doppler Radar: Velocity, Sampling & Storm Motion

days.lesson: Advance radial-velocity interpretation, aliasing, range folding, beam geometry, storm-relative concepts and sampling limitations.
Use vector projections and trigonometry to relate true motion/wind to radial velocity and storm motion.
Analyze paired reflectivity/velocity data and distinguish convergence, divergence, rotation and artifacts.
Use NWS radar products and MetEd cases to document evidence versus interpretation.
Prepare a radar-based nowcast with explicit uncertainty and no unsupported warning claims.
Study ZDR, correlation coefficient, differential phase/KDP and conceptual hydrometeor classification.
Interpret logarithmic ratios, gradients and uncertainty; compare multi-variable radar signatures.
Evaluate dual-pol signatures for heavy rain, hail, melting layer and nonmeteorological returns.
Cross-check radar interpretation with surface reports, satellite and environmental profiles.
Build a heavy-rain/hail decision-support briefing with evidence hierarchy and confidence.
Advance visible, infrared, water-vapor, near-IR and multispectral-composite interpretation for clouds, moisture and dynamics.
Relate radiance/brightness temperature, weighting functions and spatial/temporal sampling to interpretation.
Analyze cloud-top evolution, moisture gradients, fog/low cloud and upper-level features in multispectral imagery.
Use NOAA GOES imagery and compare with radar/model fields to identify consistency and gaps.
Create a satellite-led nowcast and explain which conclusions are observations versus derived interpretation.
Study primitive-equation modeling conceptually, grids, time stepping, truncation error, stability and parameterized processes.
Apply numerical Euler/Runge–Kutta ideas to ODEs; examine numerical stability and error growth.
Compare model solutions at different resolutions and identify features that are resolved versus parameterized.
Inspect model fields for convection, boundary-layer, cloud and precipitation parameterization impacts.
Write a model-guidance memo that documents resolution limits and avoids treating output as ground truth.
Introduce observation operators, background/analysis concepts, data assimilation, perturbations and ensemble design.
Use probability distributions, spread, rank concepts and ODE sensitivity to initial conditions.
Compare analyses and ensemble members to observations; identify sensitive forecast elements.
Use operational ensemble guidance to assess track/timing/threshold probabilities.
Deliver a probabilistic forecast briefing with plausible alternatives and decision thresholds.

weeks.title: SEMESTER III COMPREHENSIVE — Analysis & Forecast Operations

days.lesson: Cumulative dynamics, synoptic/mesoscale diagnosis, remote sensing and NWP synthesis.
Cumulative ODE, vector, diagnostic and numerical-method examination.
Complete an unseen multi-scale case from observations through forecast reasoning.
Integrate radar, satellite, deterministic and ensemble guidance and document contradictions.
Complete a simulated forecast shift, written discussion and oral defense. Semester III requires ≥80% at every component.

courses.title: Dynamical Meteorology II
courses.description: Waves, instability, potential vorticity, ageostrophic circulations, jet/front dynamics and multiscale interactions.

courses.title: High-Impact Weather
courses.description: Deep convection, supercells, tornadoes, hail, damaging wind, winter weather, fire weather and warning decision science.

courses.title: Tropical, Aviation & Marine Meteorology
courses.description: Tropical cyclones, aviation hazards, marine boundary layer, fog, waves, coastal weather and specialized services.

courses.title: NWP II, Ensembles & Data Assimilation
courses.description: Data assimilation, ensemble design, probabilistic guidance, calibration, post-processing, bias and model diagnostics.

courses.title: Hydrometeorology & Boundary-Layer Applications
courses.description: QPF, runoff/flood response, land-atmosphere exchange, terrain, boundary-layer processes and applied hazards.

courses.title: Operational Forecasting Practicum & Capstone
courses.description: Multi-hazard forecast shifts, partner briefings, verification, forecast discussions, capstone operations and oral defense.

days.lesson: Diagnose buoyancy, parcel choice, CAPE/CIN, lapse rates, moisture depth, forcing and convective initiation failure modes.
Calculate parcel/environment temperature differences, layer lapse rates and simplified buoyancy/CAPE relationships.
Analyze soundings, surface boundaries and forcing to assess initiation timing and conditionality.
Use radar/satellite/SPC mesoscale products and convection-allowing models to track pre-storm evolution.
Issue a conditional thunderstorm forecast with explicit triggers, failure modes and confidence.
Study storm modes, vertical shear, hodographs, storm-relative flow, mesocyclones and supercell structure.
Compute shear vectors, storm-relative wind concepts and qualitative helicity relationships.
Classify storm environment and expected mode using soundings/hodographs and boundary orientation.
Track developing convection with radar, satellite and high-resolution model guidance.
Produce a severe-weather briefing separating environmental potential from observed storm behavior.
Integrate environmental and radar evidence for tornado, hail and wind hazards; study warning decision uncertainty and false-alarm tradeoffs.
Apply probability, base-rate and conditional-risk reasoning to hazard decisions.
Analyze an archived severe-weather event and identify signal evolution, reports and decision points.
Use radar/mesoanalysis/satellite evidence while documenting artifacts and uncertainty.
Complete a simulated warning/impact decision log and partner briefing; official-warning language is clearly separated from training simulation.
Study snow/ice microphysics, warm noses, wet-bulb effects, frontogenesis, deformation bands and mesoscale snow processes.
Calculate thickness/wet-bulb approximations, thermal profiles and simple snow/liquid ratios with uncertainty.
Diagnose precipitation type, banding potential and transition zones from soundings/cross-sections.
Compare radar, satellite and ensemble guidance for band placement and precipitation-type uncertainty.
Prepare a winter-weather impact forecast including confidence ranges and bust scenarios.

weeks.title: Boundary Layer, Fire Weather & Complex Terrain

days.lesson: Study turbulent mixing, stability, diurnal boundary-layer evolution, downslope/upslope flow, gap winds and fire-weather ingredients.
Apply flux/gradient concepts, Richardson-number intuition and terrain-adjusted wind reasoning.
Analyze surface/upper-air data for mixing height, humidity recovery, wind shifts and terrain effects.
Use high-resolution guidance, satellite fire/smoke context and observations while respecting hotspot limitations.
Produce a fire-weather/terrain briefing focused on wind, humidity, stability and timing.

weeks.title: UNIT VII CHECKPOINT — High-Impact Midlatitude Weather

days.lesson: Synthesize Weeks 19–23: convection, severe hazards, winter weather, boundary layer and terrain.
Cumulative thermodynamic, kinematic and probabilistic calculations.
Complete an unseen high-impact case and identify competing hazards and uncertainties.
Integrate radar, satellite, observations and model/ensemble guidance.
Deliver a multi-hazard decision-support briefing. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.
Study tropical thermodynamics, easterly waves, vorticity, moisture, shear, ocean coupling and genesis environments.
Apply angular momentum, vorticity and thermodynamic calculations to simplified tropical systems.
Analyze a pre-genesis disturbance from satellite, surface/upper-air and environmental data.
Compare ensemble/genesis guidance and satellite organization trends.
Prepare a tropical disturbance outlook-style training brief without representing it as an official NHC product.

weeks.title: Tropical Cyclone Structure, Track, Intensity & Hazards

days.lesson: Study warm-core structure, eyewall/rainbands, steering, beta effects, shear, ocean heat, rapid intensity change and hazard asymmetry.
Use vector steering, pressure-wind reasoning and probabilistic track/intensity interpretation.
Analyze an active/archive cyclone with reconnaissance/satellite/model information where available.
Compare official NHC products with model/ensemble guidance and identify why guidance is not the official forecast.
Deliver a partner-focused tropical hazard briefing covering wind, surge, rain and tornado risk.
Study ceilings/visibility, convection, turbulence, icing, wind shear, mountain waves, jet-stream hazards and aviation forecast products.
Apply density/pressure, wind components, freezing-level and probability calculations to flight-weather problems.
Analyze METAR/TAF-style observations plus sounding/radar/satellite evidence for an aviation route/terminal.
Use Aviation Weather Center products with model and observational context.
Create a training aviation weather brief with timing, confidence and operational impacts.
Study marine boundary layer, pressure/wind over water, stability, fog, coastal jets, convection and wave-generation concepts.
Calculate wind-wave relationships conceptually, fetch/duration effects and marine pressure/wind diagnostics.
Analyze a coastal/offshore case including fronts, fog, gale potential and sea-state evolution.
Use Ocean Prediction Center, satellite, buoy/observation and model guidance.
Produce a marine forecast brief emphasizing wind, waves, visibility and hazardous transitions.
Study precipitation efficiency, training convection, terrain enhancement, antecedent conditions, runoff response and flash-flood concepts.
Apply basin-average precipitation, recurrence/probability and simple runoff/threshold calculations.
Analyze QPF, radar estimates, soil/river context and observed rainfall for a flood-risk case.
Use Weather Prediction Center and National Water Prediction Service products with radar/model guidance.
Create a flood decision-support briefing that separates meteorological forecast from hydrologic official products.

weeks.title: UNIT VIII CHECKPOINT — Specialized Forecast Services

days.lesson: Synthesize tropical, aviation, marine and hydrometeorological forecasting.
Cumulative vector/probability/diagnostic calculations across specialized services.
Complete an unseen scenario requiring service-specific analysis and hazard prioritization.
Use the appropriate official center products and observational/model evidence.
Deliver two audience-specific briefings from the same meteorological evidence. Unit checkpoint ≥80% required.

weeks.title: NWP II: Model Physics, Bias & Post-Processing

days.lesson: Examine microphysics, convection, boundary-layer and radiation schemes; identify systematic model biases and post-processing needs.
Use error statistics, regression/calibration concepts and bias correction on a small forecast dataset.
Compare multiple model forecasts against observations and quantify recurring error modes.
Inspect deterministic and ensemble guidance for physics-dependent differences.
Write a model-bias memo and adjust a forecast only when supported by evidence.
Study ensemble perturbations, data-assimilation cycles, spread-error relationships, sensitivity and predictability limits.
Calculate Brier-score style probability error, reliability concepts and ensemble summary statistics.
Evaluate an ensemble forecast for spread, clustering, outliers and observation consistency.
Use ensemble probabilities/plumes/spaghetti-style fields and compare with deterministic runs.
Issue a probabilistic decision-support forecast with threshold-based scenarios.
Translate meteorological hazards into impact-relevant information while preserving uncertainty and role boundaries.
Use decision thresholds, expected-value concepts and contingency tables to evaluate forecast usefulness.
Build an impact matrix for multiple partners with different vulnerabilities and lead-time needs.
Integrate official products, observations, forecast guidance and partner context without altering authoritative warnings.
Conduct a simulated partner briefing, questions-and-answers session and update cycle.
Study deterministic and probabilistic verification, bias, MAE/RMSE, contingency tables, reliability, resolution and skill.
Calculate verification metrics and interpret when a metric can mislead.
Verify a multi-day forecast set by variable/hazard and diagnose systematic failure modes.
Compare model and human forecast performance using consistent verification periods.
Write an after-action forecast review with specific corrective learning objectives.
Integrate the entire two-year curriculum under a simulated forecast-office workflow and shift handoff.
Complete rapid quantitative diagnostics selected from dynamics, thermodynamics, probability and verification.
Perform surface/upper-air, radar, satellite, model and ensemble analysis under a fixed briefing deadline.
Maintain a source/valid-time log and resolve conflicting guidance through documented reasoning.
Complete a full forecast shift: analysis → forecast → discussion → partner brief → verification plan → handoff.

weeks.title: YEAR II CAPSTONE — Professional Meteorologist Qualification Review

days.lesson: Complete a cumulative meteorology examination spanning dynamics, synoptic/mesoscale analysis, physical meteorology, remote sensing, NWP and specialized operations.
Complete quantitative ODE/dynamics/thermodynamics/probability/verification problems without averaging away weak domains.
Analyze an unseen multi-hazard case and document the full evidence chain.
Integrate radar, satellite, observations, deterministic/ensemble guidance and official center products.
Complete the final simulated operational shift, written forecast discussion, decision-support briefing, portfolio defense and oral examination. Every component ≥80%.
